name: Annotated diagram overlay
looks: A short hand-drawn label and arrow pop onto the exact element being demonstrated and name what it is doing. The label sits in a casual script face, distinct from the display type, so it reads as a designer's note rather than a caption bar. Only one label is on screen at a time, and each leaves before the next arrives.
build: The label is DOM text in a second handwritten or marker face with its own role; the arrow is an SVG path drawn on with strokeDashoffset and a small arrowhead that pops in at the end. Anchor each label to its element's position from the same clock so it never drifts when the element moves.
sound: A tick on each label's arrival.
prompt: Over a shot that is already demonstrating a move (a bounce, a curve, a stagger), pop a short hand-drawn label and arrow directly onto the element doing the work, naming the mechanism in a few words. Use a casual script or marker face distinct from the rest of the type, keep only one label live at a time, and have it point at the thing itself, not at empty space. Let each label arrive on the beat and clear before the next lands.
